title: The Guards Counterattack

source.basis: Adapted from a legacy card to the registered rulebook (ruling R17.2); the Chapter H DYO procedures check its numbers, and what they leave open is manufactured under R0.3.
source.legacy: ASL Scenario A, The General, Vol. 22 No. 6 (1986), p. 51
adaptation: The legacy text is paraphrased, not copied.
The legacy Russian 9-0 in N4 is the 9-0 Commissar, which A25.22 lets the Russians field in a scenario set in or before 10/42 (ruling R17.9).
The German HMG is new on sheet MFG; the German LMG and MMG and the Russian MMG were already manufactured there (R0.3; ruling R17.9).

The Victory Conditions are restated in A26 terms: the legacy 'completely occupy' becomes Control (A26.1, A26.14), which needs only an armed Good Order MMC in any hex of the building, a looser test that favors the Russians.
The legacy SSR 2, encirclement of an upper-level unit whose exit is blocked, goes beyond A7.7 and is shown, not enforced.
Each setup area lists every hex of its building on board 1, as the legacy SSR 3 lets units set up anywhere in their building.
The legacy diagram prints a bare N beside the board with no arrow; North is read as the map's top.

introduction: Early October 1942. The Germans have nearly cleared the ground around the Dzerzhinsky Tractor Works, but the line companies holding it are worn thin by a week of street fighting. A battalion of the 37th Guards Division counterattacks to break the ring and reach the factory's defenders.

playableArea.text: Only hexrows A to P are playable.

friendlyEdge.note: A20.53: in every hex column of board 1, the hexes of the German setup buildings lie south of those of the Russian ones, so the south edge is one of the German Friendly Board Edges; the game names one edge per side (R5.16).

sides.balance: Add one Hero to any German group.

friendlyEdge.note: A20.53: in every hex column of board 1, the hexes of the Russian setup buildings lie north of those of the German ones, so the north edge is one of the Russian Friendly Board Edges; the game names one edge per side (R5.16).

sides.balance: Sewers are usable (B8.1) and Russian units may use Sewer Movement (B8.4); the Germans may then enter them with a leader passing a 4TC (B8.4).

specialRules.text: EC are Moderate, with no wind at start (B25.5, B25.63); the weather is Clear (no weather SSR).
specialRules.note: The Clear weather is the game's default (R16.9); EC and wind, which matter for fire spread, are not modeled yet (backlog).

specialRules.text: An upper-level unit whose way out of the building is blocked by Good Order enemy MMC is encircled while it stays blocked, with no further penalty; a unit also encircled by fire loses that only when it has a way out and A7.7 no longer applies.
specialRules.note: It adds an encirclement that A7.7 does not have (backlog).

specialRules.text: Units may set up in any hex of their designated building.
specialRules.note: Placing the OB in its setup areas is pass 19 of the Scenario Card Games Plan.

victoryConditions.text: The Russians win if at game end they Control two more of the German setup stone buildings (F5, K5, I7, M7, and M9) than the Germans Control of the Russian setup stone buildings (N4, J2, M2, and F3; N2 is wooden and does not count), or if they then have at least three times as many unbroken squad-equivalents as the Germans. Otherwise the Germans win.
